name: Battle of Kursk
note: The plan shows the whole operation, not a single field: the formations are armies and fronts, drawn as simple blocks. The accounts give the northern face, the southern face, Orel to the north and Belgorod and Prokhorovka but not their distances, so the places are set by judgement. The Northern Donets is drawn as a line south of the 4th Panzer Army and Army Detachment Kempf; the accounts do not say exactly where it lay. Ponyri and Olkhovatka are placed on the northern face without exact positions. The 7th Guards Army, which faced Army Detachment Kempf, is not drawn apart from the Voronezh Front.

phases.title: The two armies take up their ground
phases.text: The Germans planned two pincers on the Kursk salient, the 9th Army from the north and the 4th Panzer Army with Army Detachment Kempf from the south, while the 2nd Army held the west. The Central and Voronezh Fronts stood in fortified belts, with the Steppe Front in reserve.
phases.quote: Operation Citadel called for a double envelopment to surround the Soviet defenders of five armies and seal off the Kursk salient.

phases.title: Both German pincers attack
phases.text: The 9th Army attacked the Central Front in the north, and in the south the 4th Panzer Army and Army Detachment Kempf attacked across the Voronezh Front's sector. Each broke into the first belt of the Soviet defences.
phases.quote: Following a preliminary bombardment and Red Army counter bombardments, the 9th Army opened its attack at 05:30 on 5 July.

phases.title: The northern attack is held at Ponyri and Olkhovatka
phases.text: Model put the weight of the 9th Army on Ponyri and Olkhovatka, and the Central Front counterattacked and held both. By 10 July the Soviets had completely halted the German advance in the north.
phases.quote: By 10 July, the Soviets had completely halted the German advance.

phases.title: Soviet reserves arrive and the II SS turns to Prokhorovka
phases.text: The 5th Guards Tank Army left the Steppe Front for Prokhorovka on 7 July. On 10 July Hoth turned the II SS Panzer Corps of the 4th Panzer Army north-east towards it, and on 11 July Army Detachment Kempf broke through.
phases.quote: On 7 July, the 5th Guards Tank Army began advancing to Prokhorovka.

phases.title: The tank battle at Prokhorovka
phases.text: The 5th Guards Tank Army attacked down the slopes before Prokhorovka against the II SS Panzer Corps, which was attacking on its own plan. Neither side accomplished its objectives that day.
phases.quote: Down off the west slopes, before Prokhorovka, came the massed armour of five tank brigades from the Soviet 18th and 29th Tank Corps of the 5th Guards Tank Army.

phases.title: Kutuzov opens in the north and Citadel ends in the south
phases.text: The Bryansk and Western Fronts began Operation Kutuzov against the Orel salient, threatening the 9th Army's flank and rear, so that it went over fully to the defensive. In the south the II SS Panzer Corps was ordered on 17 July to end its offensive and begin to withdraw.
phases.quote: As the German momentum in the north slowed, the Soviets launched Operation Kutuzov on 12 July against Army Group Centre in the Orel salient, directly north of the Kursk salient.

phases.title: Operation Rumyantsev drives south to Belgorod
phases.text: The Voronezh and Steppe Fronts attacked the northern wing of Army Group South, aiming to destroy the 4th Panzer Army and Army Detachment Kempf. They drove through the German positions and by 5 August had liberated Belgorod.
phases.quote: The offensive was initiated by the Voronezh Front and Steppe Fronts against the northern wing of Army Group South.
